Input

What can I use Langfuse for?

Output

Here’s what teams use Langfuse for:

  • Observability & application tracing

    • Capture structured traces of every LLM/tool/retrieval step; inspect prompts, outputs, token usage, cost, and latency; group multi-turn flows into sessions; debug via timelines and agent graphs; monitor with dashboards and alerts
    • Docs: Observability overview https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/overview, Core concepts https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/data-model, Best practices https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/best-practices

  • Prompt management

    • Version, test in a playground, deploy via labels (no code change), compare cost/latency/quality across versions, and link prompts to traces
    • Docs: Prompt management overview https://langfuse.com/docs/prompt-management/overview

  • Evaluation

    • Measure quality with scores (LLM-as-a-judge, code evaluators, user feedback, manual annotations), run experiments on datasets (offline), and score production traffic (online)
    • Docs: Evaluation overview https://langfuse.com/docs/evaluation/overview, Core concepts https://langfuse.com/docs/evaluation/core-concepts

  • Platform & integrations

    • API-first SDKs (Python/JS), 100+ integrations and OpenTelemetry ingestion, data export to blob storage, RBAC/SSO, self-host or cloud
    • Docs: Overview https://langfuse.com/docs

Minimal example: ingest your first trace (Python, OpenAI wrapper)

  • Get started: https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/get-started

  1. Install pip install langfuse

  2. Set env vars LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-... LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-... LANGFUSE_BASE_URL=https://cloud.langfuse.com

  3. Use the wrapped OpenAI client from langfuse.openai import openai

completion = openai.chat.completions.create( name="test-chat", model="gpt-4o", messages=[ {"role": "system", "content": "You are a very accurate calculator."}, {"role": "user", "content": "1 + 1 = "} ], metadata={"someMetadataKey": "someValue"}, )

  • Observability & application tracing

    • Docs: Observability overview https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/overview, Core concepts https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/data-model, Best practices https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/best-practices

  • Prompt management

    • Version, test in a playground, deploy via labels (no code change), compare cost/latency/quality across versions, and link prompts to traces
    • Docs: Prompt management overview https://langfuse.com/docs/prompt-management/overview

  • Evaluation

    • Measure quality with scores (LLM-as-a-judge, code evaluators, user feedback, manual annotations), run experiments on datasets (offline), and score production traffic (online)

  • Get started: https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/get-started

  2. Set env vars LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-... LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-... LANGFUSE_BASE_URL=https://cloud.langfuse.com

  3. Use the wrapped OpenAI client from langfuse.openai import openai

{"type": "text", "text": "# Langfuse\n\n> Langfuse is an **open-source AI engineering platform** ([GitHub](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse)) that helps teams collaboratively debug, analyze, and iterate on their LLM applications. All platform features are natively integrated to accelerate the development workflow.\n\n## Markdown Access\n\nEvery page on langfuse.com is available as plain Markdown. Append `.md` to any URL, or send an `Accept: text/markdown` header:\n\n```bash\ncurl https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/get-started.md\n```\n\nThe links in the section indexes below already point at the `.md` variants.\n\n## Docs Search API\n\nSemantic search (RAG) over the Langfuse documentation, returning an answer with the relevant pages and excerpts. No authentication required. Use this instead of guessing when a specific page does not answer the question:\n\n```bash\ncurl -sG \"https://langfuse.com/api/search-docs\" --data-urlencode \"query=How do I trace a LangGraph agent?\"\n```\n\n- **Endpoint**: `https://langfuse.com/api/search-docs?query=<question>`\n- **Documentation**: [REST endpoint](https://langfuse.com/docs/docs-mcp#rest-endpoint)\n\nAsk specific, self-contained questions in natural language. This is the same search that backs the `searchLangfuseDocs` MCP tool below.\n\n## Langfuse Docs MCP Server\n\nConnect to the Langfuse Docs MCP server to access documentation directly in your AI editor:\n\n- **Endpoint**: `https://langfuse.com/api/mcp`\n- **Transport**: `streamableHttp`\n- **Documentation**: [Langfuse Docs MCP Server](https://langfuse.com/docs/docs-mcp)\n\nThe MCP server provides tools to search Langfuse documentation, GitHub issues, and discussions. See the [installation guide](https://langfuse.com/docs/docs-mcp) for setup instructions in Cursor, VS Code, Claude Desktop, and other MCP clients.\n\n## Langfuse Skill for AI Coding Agents\n\nInstall the Langfuse skill before implementing anything with Langfuse. The skill provides up-to-date documentation, best-practice workflows for instrumentation, prompt management, and programmatic API access via the Langfuse CLI.\n\nInstall from: [github.com/langfuse/skills](https://github.com/langfuse/skills/tree/main/skills/langfuse)\n\n## Tracing Best Practices\n\nBefore instrumenting an application with Langfuse, read [What does a good trace look like?](https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/best-practices.md) — it covers trace scope, observation naming, meaningful input/output, and the attributes (metadata, tags, users, sessions) that evaluators, dashboards, and experiments rely on.\n\n## Docs\n\nFor the best results, install the [Langfuse skill](https://github.com/langfuse/skills/tree/main/skills/langfuse) before using these {"type": "text", "text": "{\"content\": [{\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/data-model\", \"title\": \"Core Concepts\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Concepts - Langfuse\\n[Docs](/docs)\\n[Observability](/docs/observability/overview)\\n[Concepts](/docs/observability/data-model)\\n# Core Concepts\\nThis page digs into the underlying concepts of how Langfuse structures and captures your data. Understanding these will make debugging and working with traces easier.\\nReady to start? Check out the [Get Started guide](/docs/observability/get-started) to ingest your first trace.\\n## Observations, Traces, and Sessions\\nLangfuse organizes an application's data into three core concepts: observations, traces, and sessions.\\nSession\\nTrace\\nObservation\\nObservation\\nObservation\\nTrace\\nObservation\\nObservation\\nObservation\\nObservation\\nTrace\\nObservation\\nObservation\\n### Observations & Traces\\n`Observations` are the individual steps of your application: LLM calls, tool calls, retrieval steps, and so on. They can be nested to reflect the structure of your application, and Langfuse supports several LLM-specific [observation types](/docs/observability/features/observation-types) such as _generations_ and _events_.\\nA `trace` represents a single request or operation, for example one chatbot interaction from the user's question to the final response. It is the logical grouping of all observations that share the same `trace_id`.\\nTrace-level attributes such as `user_id`, `session_id`, `tags`, and `metadata` live on every observation within the trace; the SDKs propagate them automatically. Conceptually, Langfuse stores one observations table, and each row holds the observation-level data plus a copy of the trace-level attributes. This keeps queries and aggregations fast:\\nObservations table\\nObservation-level data| Trace-level data · on every row \\n---|--- \\nid| type| name| latency| trace_id| trace_name| user_id| session_id \\nobs-1| span| handle-chat| 3.1s| abc123| chat-request| u-42| s-7 \\nobs-2| span| retrieval| 0.4s| abc123| chat-request| u-42| s-7 \"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/overview\", \"title\": \"Observability & Application Tracing\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"LLM Observability & Application Tracing (Open Source) - Langfuse\\n[Docs](/docs)\\n[Observability](/docs/observability/overview)\\n[Overview](/docs/observability/overview)\\n# Observability & Application Tracing\\nGenerative AI systems are inherently non-deterministic. Therefore, debugging your application without any observability tool is more like guesswork. Implementing comprehensive AI observability gives you the tools to understand what's happening inside your application and why. It is the foundation for continuously evaluating and improving your system.\\nThe core of this is **application tracing** — structured logs of every request that capture the exact prompt sent, the model's response, token usage, latency, and any tools or retrieval steps in between.\\nHere's an example of a trace in the Langfuse UI:\\n🚀\\nWant to see it in action? [**Create a free account**](/cloud) and explore Langfuse Observability in the [interactive example project](/docs/demo).\\n## Getting Started\\nStart by [setting up your first trace](/docs/observability/get-started), and compare it against our [best practices guide](/docs/observability/best-practices) so you're set up for success. If you're new to AI observability, take a look at the [core concepts](/docs/observability/data-model) too.\\n## Use your traces\\nOnce traces are coming in, the next step is to make sense of them and use what you learn to improve your agent. Read the chapter on [Monitoring in the Langfuse Academy](/academy/monitoring) to learn how to utilize your traces well.\\nFor feature-specific implementation guidance, these are the most common ones to start with:\\n * Track [model usage and cost](/docs/observability/features/token-and-cost-tracking)\\n * Monitor application quality with [scores](/docs/evaluation/scores/overview)\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/docs\", \"title\": \"Langfuse Overview\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Overview - Langfuse\\n[Docs](/docs)\\n[Overview](/docs)\\n# Langfuse Overview\\nLangfuse is an open-source AI engineering platform ([GitHub](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse)) that helps teams collaboratively debug, analyze, and iterate on their AI agent applications. All platform features are natively integrated to accelerate the development workflow. Langfuse is open, self-hostable, and extensible ([ _why Langfuse?_](/why)).\\n### Observability\\n * Log traces\\n * Lowest level transparency\\n * Understand cost and latency\\n### Prompts\\n * Version control and deploy\\n * Collaborate on prompts\\n * Test prompts and models\\n### Evaluation\\n * Measure output quality\\n * Monitor production health\\n * Test changes in development\\n### Platform\\n * API-first architecture\\n * Data exports to blob storage\\n * Enterprise security and administration\\n## Observability\\n[Observability](/docs/observability/overview) is essential for understanding and debugging AI agent applications. Unlike traditional software, AI agent applications involve complex, non-deterministic interactions that can be challenging to monitor and debug. Langfuse provides comprehensive tracing capabilities that help you understand exactly what's happening in your application.\\n * Traces include all LLM and non-LLM calls, including retrieval, embedding, API calls, and more\\n * Support for tracking multi-turn conversations as sessions and user tracking\\n * Agents can be represented as graphs\\n * Capture traces via our native SDKs for Python/JS, 100+ library/framework integrations, OpenTelemetry, or via an LLM Gateway such as LiteLLM\\n * Based on OpenTelemetry to increase compatibility and reduce vendor lock-in\\n🚀\\nWant to see it in action?\\n[Create a free account](/cloud) and explore Langfuse Observability in the [interactive example project](/docs/demo).\\nTrace DetailsSessionsTimelineUsersAgent GraphsDashboardAlerts\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nTraces allow you to track every LLM call and other relevant logic in your app.\\nSessions allow you to track multi-step conversations or agentic workflows.\\nDebug latency issues by inspecting the timeline view.\\nAdd your own `userId` to monitor costs and usage for each user. Optionally, create a deep link to this view in your systems.\\nLLM agents can be visualized as a graph to illustrate the flow of complex agentic workflows.\\nSee quality, cost, and latency metrics in the dashboard to monitor your LLM application.\\nGet notified over Slack, GitHub Actions, or Webhooks when a metric crosses a threshold with [alerts](/docs/observability/features/alerts).\\n## Prompt Management\\n[Prompt Management](/docs/prompt-management/overview) is critical in building effective AI applications. Langfuse provides tools to help you manage, version, and optimize your prompts throughout the development lifecycle.\\n * [Get started](/docs/prompt-management/get-started) with prompt management\\n * Manage, version, and optimize your prompts throughout the development lifecycle\\n * Test prompts interactively in the [LLM Playground](/docs/prompt-management/features/playground)\\n * Run [Experiments](/docs/evaluation/features/prompt-experiments) against datasets to test new prompt versions directly within Langfuse\\n🚀\\nWant to see it in action? [**Create a free account**](/cloud) and explore Langfuse Prompt Management in the [interactive example project](/docs/demo).\\nCreateVersion ControlDeployMetricsTest in PlaygroundLink with TracesTrack Changes\\nCreate a new prompt via UI, SDKs, or API.\\nCollaboratively version and edit prompts via UI, API, or SDKs.\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nDeploy prompts to production or any environment via labels - without any code changes.\\nCompare latency, cost, and evaluation metrics across different versions of your prompts.\\nInstantly test your prompts in the playground.\\nLink prompts with traces to understand how they perform in the context of your LLM application.\\nTrack changes to your prompts to understand how they evolve over time.\\n## Evaluation\\n[Evaluation](/docs/evaluation/overview) is crucial for ensuring the quality and reliability of your LLM applications. Langfuse provides flexible evaluation tools that adapt to your specific needs, whether you're testing in development or monitoring production performance.\\n * Get started with different [evaluation methods](/docs/evaluation/overview): LLM-as-a-judge, code evaluators, user feedback, manual labeling, or custom pipelines\\n * Identify issues early by running evaluations on production traces\\n * Create and manage [Datasets](/docs/evaluation/features/datasets) for systematic testing in development that ensure your application performs reliably across different scenarios\\n * Run [Experiments](/docs/evaluation/core-concepts#experiments) to systematically test your LLM application\\n🚀\\nWant to see it in action? [**Create a free account**](/cloud) and explore Langfuse Evaluation in the [interactive example project](/docs/demo).\\nAnalyticsUser FeedbackLLM-as-a-JudgeExperimentsAnnotation QueueCustom Evals\\nPlot evaluation results in the Langfuse Dashboard.\\nCollect feedback from your users. Can be captured in the frontend via our Browser SDK, server-side via the SDKs or API. Video includes example application.\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nRun fully managed LLM-as-a-judge evaluations on production or development traces. Can be applied to any step within your application for step-wise evaluations.\\nEvaluate prompts and models on datasets directly in the user interface. No custom code is needed.\\nBaseline your evaluation workflow with human annotations via Annotation Queues.\\nAdd custom evaluation results, supports numeric, boolean and categorical values.\\n \\n \\n```\\nPOST /api/public/scores\\n```\\nAdd scores via Python or JS SDK.\\nExample (Python)\\n \\n \\n```\\nlangfuse.score(\\n trace_id=\\\"123\\\",\\n name=\\\"my_custom_evaluator\\\",\\n value=0.5,\\n)\\n```\\n## Where to start?\\nSetting up the full process of online tracing, prompt management, production evaluations to identify issues, and offline evaluations on datasets requires some time. Most teams eventually end up with a process that looks like this:\\nDeploy\\n[OnlineTracetraces · sessions · agents · prompts](/academy/tracing)\\n[OnlineMonitordashboards · LLM-as-judge · feedback](/academy/monitoring)\\n[OfflineBuild datasetsdatasets · features-as-tests](/academy/datasets)\\n[OfflineExperimentprompts · models · code variants](/academy/experiments)\\n[OfflineEvaluatejudges · custom evals · annotation](/academy/evaluate)\\nIf you're new to AI engineering, take a look at the [Academy](/academy), where you'll find conceptual guidance on how to approach AI engineering, trade-offs, and best practices. If you already know what you want, the getting-started guides below will get you going.\\n💡\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nTip: let your coding agent do the setup and work with Langfuse through the [Agent Skill](/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/agent-skill), [CLI](/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/cli), or [MCP server](/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/mcp-server). On Langfuse Cloud, you can also ask the [Langfuse Assistant](/docs/langfuse-assistant) about your project data from inside the app.\\n## Quickstarts\\nGet up and running with Langfuse in minutes. Choose the path that best fits your current needs:\\n[\\n### Integrate LLM Application/Agent Tracing\\n](/docs/observability/get-started)\\n[\\n### Integrate Prompt Management\\n](/docs/prompt-management/get-started)\\n[\\n### Setup Evaluations\\n](/docs/evaluation/overview)\\n## Why Langfuse?\\n * **Open source:** Fully open source with public API for custom integrations\\n * **Production optimized:** Designed with minimal performance overhead\\n * **Best-in-class SDKs:** Native SDKs for Python and JavaScript\\n * **Framework support:** Integrated with popular frameworks like OpenAI SDK, LangChain, and LlamaIndex\\n * **Multi-modal:** Support for tracing text, images and other modalities\\n * **Full platform:** Suite of tools for the complete LLM application development lifecycle\\n## Community & Contact\\nWe actively develop Langfuse in [open source](/open-source) together with our community:\\n * Contribute and vote on the Langfuse [roadmap](/docs/roadmap).\\n * Ask questions on [GitHub Discussions](/gh-support) or private [support channels](/support).\\n * Report bugs via [GitHub Issues](/issue).\\n * Chat with the community on [Discord](/discord).\\n * Join a [community hour](/events) to talk to the team and ask questions live.\\n * [Why people choose Langfuse?](/why)\\nLangfuse evolves quickly, check out the [changelog](/changelog) for the latest updates. Subscribe to the **mailing list** to get notified about new major features:\\nSubscribe\\n* * *\\n* * *\\nLast edited 9/1/2026\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"site\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/users/ravenna\", \"title\": \"How Ravenna uses Langfuse to build and debug AI agents for enterprise internal support - Langfuse\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"---\\n\\nWe value your privacy\\nWe use cookies to enhance your browsing experience, serve personalised ads or content, and analyse our traffic. pages.\\n\\n---\\n\\n__\\nAnalytics\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nAnalytical cookies are used to understand how visitors interact with the website. (Terraform)\\n](/self-hosting/deployment/azure)\\n\\n---\\n\\nJuly 24, 2026\\n# How Ravenna uses Langfuse to build and debug AI agents for enterprise internal support\\nLearn how Ravenna uses Langfuse for end-to-end observability and evals across their AI-native internal service desk, enabling engineers and CS teams to debug agentic workflows orders of magnitude faster.\\nFelix\\nAnnabell\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Preface\\n\\n---\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nWhen someone at Langfuse has an IT Support request, they head to the #it-support channel, formulate their request and get immediate help. Help powered by Ravenna’s IT support automation agents. And Ravenna's agents run reliably because Ravenna runs on Langfuse.\\n## About Ravenna\\n\\n---\\n\\n[Ravenna](https://www.ravenna.ai/) builds an AI-native internal service desk where human agents and AI agents collaborate on employee support tickets. IT, HR, and revenue operations teams can use Ravenna to build agents that automate their work. The platform lives primarily in Slack and includes a full-stack ticketing system, an automation engine integrated with core business systems, and a reporting suite.\\n\\n---\\n\\nRavenna challenges incumbents like ServiceNow, Jira Service Management, and Freshservice. The difference: Ravenna built the entire platform AI-first from the ground up rather than bolting AI onto legacy software. Agents are first-class citizens of the architecture, not add-ons.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## From RAG chatbot to agentic platform\\nWhen Ravenna started in 2024, customer expectations were simple: hook into a knowledge base and answer questions in Slack.\\nThat changed fast. By 2026, customers had seen what Claude, Perplexity, and computer-use agents could do. The expectation changed from simple replies that might describe how to go about something to agents that take that very action for you, ideally in seconds, ideally without mistakes. People want their access permissions handled, to order new IT devices, or (a very popular one in the Langfuse team) get an email alias provisioned.\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nRavenna now offers agents that meet those expectations. They handle conversational form filling with disambiguation logic (\\\"there are 52 Johns, which one?\\\"), and even generate integrations from API docs on the fly through a tool called Foundry. A key ingredient to get there was to get deep insights into what their agents are doing, which tools they are using and which challenges they have to solve. Something that was possible by integrating Langfuse from day 1.\\n## Why Langfuse was adopted from day one\\nTaylor Halliday, Ravenna's co-founder and CEO, was previously Director of AI Engineering at Zapier and had a clear conviction going in: the core principles of good software engineering, test-driven development and observability, got somehow abandoned when AI arrived. Everyone was vibing their way to production. Something that was not an option for him when building Ravenna.\\nThere was no \\\"we tried building internal tools first\\\" phase. Langfuse was chosen before the first agent shipped because building Ravenna without LLM observability would have been impossible. When your agents handle sensitive enterprise workflows across IT, HR, and operations, face new contexts, policies and integrations in every company, you need to see exactly what they are doing and why.\\n**Why Ravenna chose Langfuse specifically:**\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Open source with a path to[self-hosting](/self-hosting).** Ravenna handles sensitive enterprise data and hooks into customers' core business systems. While the team is running on Langfuse Cloud, the ability to eventually deploy Langfuse in customer VPCs was a key factor.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Clean, well-built product.** No friction, no annoyances.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Right price point.** Appropriately priced for a growing startup shipping fast.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## How Ravenna uses Langfuse\\n### Tracing is everything\\n\\n---\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"site\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/blog/product-analytics-for-LLM-apps\", \"title\": \"Launch YC - Langfuse Blog\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"---\\n\\n[TypeScript SDK v4 GA →Langfuse TypeScript SDK v4 is here →](/changelog/2025-08-28-typescript-sdk-v4-ga)\\n\\n---\\n\\n[](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse \\\"GitHub Repository\\\")\\n\\n---\\n\\nJul 19, 2023\\n# Langfuse — Open source product analytics for LLM applications\\nThis is a cross-post of our Launch YC (W23) which explains why we're building Langfuse.\\n\\n---\\n\\n[Clemens](https://twitter.com/rawert)\\n\\n---\\n\\n[Marc](https://twitter.com/marcklingen)\\n\\n---\\n\\n[Max](https://twitter.com/maxdeichmann)\\n\\n---\\n\\n_**TLDR:** Langfuse is building open source product analytics (think ‘Mixpanel’) for LLM apps. We help companies to track and analyze quality, cost and latency across product releases and use cases._\\n\\n---\\n\\nHi everyone,\\nwe’re Max, Marc and Clemens. We were part of the Winter 23 batch and work on Langfuse, where we help teams make sense of how their LLM applications perform.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 🤯 Problem\\n\\n---\\n\\nLLMs represent a new paradigm in software. Single LLM calls are probabilistic and add substantial latency and cost. Applications use LLMs in new ways via advanced prompting, embedding-based retrieval, chains, and agents with tools. Teams building production-grade LLM applications have new **product analytics** and **monitoring** needs:\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Quality of outputs** is difficult to measure. Outputs can e.g. be inaccurate, unhelpful, poorly formatted, hallucinated or error.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Cost of compute** is a priority again given high inference costs.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Latency of responses** matters for synchronous use cases.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Debugging is challenging** due to increasingly complex LLM applications (chains, agents, tool usage).\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Understanding user behavior** is difficult given open-ended user prompts and conversational interactions.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 🧠 Solution\\n\\n---\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nLangfuse derives actionable insights from production data. Our customers use Langfuse to answer questions such as: _“How helpful are my LLM app’s outputs? What is my LLM API spend by customer? What do latencies look like across geographies and steps of LLM chains? Did the quality of the application improve in newer versions? What was the impact of switching from zero-shotting GPT4 to using few-shotted Llama calls?”_\\n\\n---\\n\\n#### Metrics\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Quality** is measured through user feedback, model-based scoring and human-in-the-loop scored samples. Quality is assessed over time as well as across prompt versions, LLMs and users.\\n * **Cost and Latency** are accurately measured and broken down by user, session, geography, feature, model and prompt version.\\n\\n---\\n\\n#### Insights\\n\\n---\\n\\n * Monitor quality/cost/latency **tradeoffs** by release to facilitate product and engineering decisions.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Cluster use cases** by employing a classifier to understand what users are doing.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * Break down **LLM usage by customer** for usage-based billing and profitability analysis.\\n\\n---\\n\\n#### Integrations\\n\\n---\\n\\n * [Python](/docs/sdk/python) and [Typescript](/docs/sdk/typescript/guide) SDKs to easily monitor complex LLM apps\\n * [Frontend SDK](/docs/sdk/typescript/guide) to directly capture feedback from users as a quality signal\\n\\n---\\n\\n_Langfuse can be self-hosted or used with a generous free tier in our managed cloud version._\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 🚧 Debugging UI\\n\\n---\\n\\nBased on the ingested data, Langfuse helps developers debug complex LLM apps in production:\\n\\n---\\n\\n * Inspect LLM app executions in a nested UI for chains, agents and tool usage.\\n * Segment by user feedback to find the root cause of quality problems.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 🙏 Asks\\n\\n---\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"site\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/enterprise\", \"title\": \"Langfuse for Enterprise - Langfuse\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nHere are our general SLOs of our support for our Enterprise Cloud customers. These can be customized upon request.\\n **Severity Levels:**\\n\\n---\\n\\n * High (Sev 1): production downtime as a fault of Langfuse, critical security issues.\\n * Medium (Sev 2): major functionality degraded for customer.\\n * Low (Sev 3): minor defect, cosmetic issue, general inquiry / support.\\n\\n---\\n\\n**Coverage Hours:**\\n\\n---\\n\\n * High Severity: 24/7 support, including weekends and holidays.\\n * Medium/Low Priority: Business hours (Monday–Friday, 09:00–21:00 Langfuse local time, excluding announced holidays).\\n\\n---\\n\\n**Acknowledgement Targets:**\\n\\n---\\n\\n * High Priority: Within 1 hour.\\n * Medium Priority: Within 24 business hours.\\n * Low Priority: Within 48 business hours.\\n\\n---\\n\\n**Resolution Targets:**\\n\\n---\\n\\n * High Priority: Continuous effort until resolved or a suitable workaround is in place, with updates every 2 hours.\\n * Medium Priority: Addressed in the next maintenance release or hot-fix, with updates on progress.\\n * Low Priority: Scheduled for the regular development cycle, with updates provided upon release.\\n\\n---\\n\\nUptime SLA for our enterprise customers\\nOur Enterprise Cloud customers get an uptime SLA:\\n * Guaranteed 99.9% uptime\\n * 99.00% to 99.89% inclusive - 10% credit\\n * Less than 99% - 20% credit\\nIf Langfuse fails to maintain an uptime percentage of greater than 99% for any 3 months in a 6 month period, Customer may terminate their agreement upon 10 days written notice to Langfuse. The calculations of uptime do not include: Delays to data ingestion or scheduled maintenance.\\n\\n---\\n\\nWhat is the difference between Langfuse Cloud and the open-source version?\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nThe Langfuse team provides Langfuse Cloud as a managed solution to simplify the initial setup of Langfuse and to minimize the operational overhead of maintaining high availability in production. You can chose to self-host Langfuse on your own infrastructure.\\nSome features are not available in the open-source version. Please refer to the overview [here](/pricing-self-host).\\n\\n---\\n\\nHow does Authentication and RBAC work in Langfuse?\\nLangfuse offers a list of prebuilt roles which apply on an organizational and project level to restrict access ([RBAC documentation](/docs/rbac)).\\nIf needed, environments (production, staging, development) can be separated into different projects in Langfuse to restrict access to production/sensitive data while making it easier to share development environments with the team and other stakeholders.\\nSSO with Langfuse is simple. Currently Google, GitHub, Azure AD, Okta, Auth0, and AWS Cognito are supported. We can easily add additional providers based on your requirements. As an enterprise customer, you can also enforce SSO for your organization.\\n\\n---\\n\\nWhat is the easiest way to try Langfuse?\\nThe Hobby Plan on [Langfuse Cloud](https://cloud.langfuse.com) includes enough resources to try Langfuse for free while in a non-production environment, no credit card required.\\nAlternatively, you can quickly spin up Langfuse on your own machine using `docker compose up` ([docs](/self-hosting/deployment/docker-compose)).\\nIf you require security and compliance features to run a POC, please reach out to us at [enterprise@langfuse.com](mailto:enterprise@langfuse.com).\\n\\n---\\n\\nCommon Enterprise LLM Platform Architecture\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nLangfuse aims to address the challenges of debugging, monitoring, and continuously improving LLM-based applications. It focuses on observability, evaluation, and prompt management.\\nLangfuse is often deployed alongside a central LLM Gateway that provides schema translation, rate limiting, and PII redaction. The LLM Gateway can be an internal service or an open-source project like LiteLLM. If you use LiteLLM, you can leverage the native integration ([docs](/integrations/gateways/litellm)).\\n\\n---\\n\\n[](/support)\\n\\n---\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/integrations/frameworks/amazon-agentcore\", \"title\": \"Integration: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Open Source Observability for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore - Langfuse\\n[Integrations](/integrations)\\n[Frameworks](/integrations/frameworks/agno-agents)\\n[Amazon Bedrock AgentCore](/integrations/frameworks/amazon-agentcore)\\n# Integration: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore\\n> **What is Amazon Bedrock AgentCore?** [Amazon Bedrock AgentCore](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agents/) is a managed service that enables you to build, deploy, and manage AI agents in production. It provides containerized agent runtimes that can execute complex workflows, use tools, and interact with external APIs while leveraging foundation models from Amazon Bedrock.\\n> **What is Langfuse?** [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/) is an open-source platform for LLM engineering. It provides tracing and monitoring capabilities for AI agents, helping developers debug, analyze, and optimize their products. Langfuse integrates with various tools and frameworks via native integrations, OpenTelemetry, and SDKs.\\n## Get Started\\nThis guide shows you how to integrate Langfuse with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to trace your agent executions using OpenTelemetry.\\n### Step 1: Install Dependencies\\nInstall the required Python packages for building and deploying AgentCore agents with Langfuse tracing:\\n \\n \\n```\\npip install bedrock-agentcore-starter-toolkit strands-agents[otel] langfuse boto3 mcp\\n```\\n### Step 2: Set Up Environment Variables\\nConfigure your AWS and Langfuse credentials:\\n **2.1 Configure Langfuse Credentials and OTEL Exporter**\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport os\\nimport base64\\n///# Get keys for your project from the project settings page: https://cloud.langfuse.com\\nos.environ.setdefault(\\\"LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY\\\", \\\"pk-lf-...\\\");\\nos.environ.setdefault(\\\"LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY\\\", \\\"sk-lf-...\\\");\\nos.environ.setdefault(\\\"LANGFUSE_BASE_URL\\\", \\\"https://cloud.langfuse.com\\\"); ///# 🇪🇺 EU region (default)\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n///# Other Langfuse data regions include 🇺🇸 US: https://us.cloud.langfuse.com, 🇯🇵 Japan: https://jp.cloud.langfuse.com and ⚕️ HIPAA: https://hipaa.cloud.langfuse.com\\n///# Build Basic Auth header for OTEL\\nlangfuse_auth = base64.b64encode(\\n f\\\"{os.environ['LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY']}:{os.environ['LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY']}\\\".encode()\\n).decode()\\n///# Configure OpenTelemetry endpoint & headers\\nos.environ[\\\"OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT\\\"] = os.environ[\\\"LANGFUSE_BASE_URL\\\"] + \\\"/api/public/otel\\\"\\nos.environ[\\\"OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS\\\"] = f\\\"Authorization=Basic {langfuse_auth},x-langfuse-ingestion-version=4\\\"\\n```\\n **2.2 Configure AWS Credentials**\\nSet your AWS credentials for accessing Bedrock services:\\n \\n \\n```\\nos.environ[\\\"AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID\\\"] = \\\"...\\\"\\nos.environ[\\\"AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY\\\"] = \\\"...\\\"\\nos.environ[\\\"AWS_DEFAULT_REGION\\\"] = \\\"us-west-2\\\"\\n```\\n### Step 3: Create Agent with Langfuse Tracing\\nCreate an AgentCore agent that integrates with Langfuse via OpenTelemetry. This example uses the Strands Agents SDK with MCP tools. Any other agent framework can be used with Langfuse, see [integration pages](/integrations) for guides on how to instrument other frameworks.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom bedrock_agentcore.runtime import BedrockAgentCoreApp\\nfrom strands import Agent\\nfrom strands.models import BedrockModel\\nfrom strands.telemetry import StrandsTelemetry\\nfrom mcp.client.streamable_http import streamablehttp_client\\nfrom strands.tools.mcp.mcp_client import MCPClient\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\n///# Initialize MCP client for tool access\\nstreamable_http_mcp_client = MCPClient(\\n lambda: streamablehttp_client(\\\"https://langfuse.com/api/mcp\\\")\\n)\\n///# Configure Bedrock model\\nbedrock_model = BedrockModel(\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n model_id=\\\"us.anthropic.claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219-v1:0\\\",\\n region_name=\\\"us-west-2\\\",\\n temperature=0.0,\\n max_tokens=4096\\n)\\n///# Define system prompt\\nsystem_prompt = \\\"\\\"\\\"You are an experienced agent supporting developers with\\nquestions about Langfuse and LLM observability.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\napp = BedrockAgentCoreApp()\\n@app.entrypoint\\ndef agent_entrypoint(payload):\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Agent entrypoint with Langfuse tracing\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n user_input = payload.get(\\\"prompt\\\")\\n trace_id = payload.get(\\\"trace_id\\\")\\n parent_obs_id = payload.get(\\\"parent_obs_id\\\")\\n # Initialize Strands telemetry and setup OTLP exporter\\n strands_telemetry = StrandsTelemetry()\\n strands_telemetry.setup_otlp_exporter()\\n # Create agent with MCP tools\\n with streamable_http_mcp_client:\\n mcp_tools = streamable_http_mcp_client.list_tools_sync()\\n agent = Agent(\\n model=bedrock_model,\\n system_prompt=system_prompt,\\n tools=mcp_tools\\n )\\n # Execute within Langfuse trace context\\n with get_client().start_as_current_observation(\\n name='agentcore-agent',\\n trace_context={\\n \\\"trace_id\\\": trace_id,\\n \\\"parent_observation_id\\\": parent_obs_id\\n }\\n ):\\n response = agent(user_input)\\n return response.message['content'][0]['text']\\nif __name__ == \\\"__main__\\\":\\n app.run()\\n```\\n### Step 4: Deploy and Invoke Agent\\nDeploy your agent to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and invoke it with trace context:\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom bedrock_agentcore_starter_toolkit import Runtime\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\nimport boto3\\nimport json\\n///# Deploy agent\\nruntime = Runtime()\\nruntime.configure(\\n entrypoint=\\\"./agent.py\\\",\\n auto_create_execution_role=True,\\n auto_create_ecr=True,\\n agent_name=\\\"langfuse-traced-agent\\\",\\n memory_mode='NO_MEMORY'\\n)\\nlaunch_result = runtime.launch(\\n env_vars={\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n \\\"DISABLE_ADOT_OBSERVABILITY\\\": \\\"true\\\", ///# Required: disable ADOT to use Langfuse\\n \\\"BEDROCK_MODEL_ID\\\": \\\"us.anthropic.claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219-v1:0\\\",\\n \\\"OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT\\\": os.environ[\\\"OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT\\\"],\\n \\\"OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS\\\": os.environ[\\\"OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS\\\"],\\n \\\"LANGFUSE_PROJECT_NAME\\\": \\\"your-project-name\\\",\\n \\\"SYSTEM_PROMPT\\\": system_prompt\\n }\\n)\\n///# Invoke agent with trace context\\nclient = boto3.client('bedrock-agentcore', region_name='us-west-2')\\n///# Get current trace context from Langfuse\\ntrace_id = get_client().get_current_trace_id()\\nobs_id = get_client().get_current_observation_id()\\npayload = json.dumps({\\n \\\"prompt\\\": \\\"What is Langfuse and how does it help monitor LLM applications?\\\",\\n \\\"trace_id\\\": trace_id,\\n \\\"parent_obs_id\\\": obs_id\\n}).encode()\\nresponse = client.invoke_agent_runtime(\\n agentRuntimeArn=launch_result.agent_arn,\\n runtimeSessionId=\\\"session-123\\\",\\n payload=payload\\n)\\n```\\n### Step 5: View Traces in Langfuse\\nAfter running your agent, log in to [Langfuse](https://cloud.langfuse.com) to explore the generated traces. You will see:\\n * Complete agent execution flows\\n * LLM calls with token counts and costs\\n * Tool usage and MCP interactions\\n * Latency metrics at each step\\n * Input/output data for debugging\\nThe traces provide comprehensive visibility into your agent's behavior in production.\\n## Using AgentCore with Other Frameworks\\nIf you're using LangChain, LlamaIndex, or another framework on AgentCore: Langfuse SDK callbacks alone won't work on AgentCore. The AgentCore runtime manages telemetry at a level that can bypass SDK HTTP calls.\\nPass these environment variables when launching your AgentCore runtime:\\n \\n \\n```\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n///# Disable AWS's built-in tracing\\nDISABLE_ADOT_OBSERVABILITY=true\\n///# Configure OTEL to export to Langfuse\\nOTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=\\\"https://cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel\\\"\\nOTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS=\\\"Authorization=Basic $(echo -n 'pk-xxx:sk-xxx' | base64),x-langfuse-ingestion-version=4\\\"\\n```\\nFor other regions, replace the endpoint host accordingly: `https://us.cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel` (US), `https://jp.cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel` (Japan), or `https://hipaa.cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel` (HIPAA).\\nHere's an example of how to launch an AgentCore runtime with the required environment variables:\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport base64\\n///# Prepare auth header\\nlangfuse_auth = base64.b64encode(\\n f\\\"{LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY}:{LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY}\\\".encode()\\n).decode()\\n///# Launch with required env vars\\nlaunch_result = agentcore_runtime.launch(\\n env_vars={\\n \\\"DISABLE_ADOT_OBSERVABILITY\\\": \\\"true\\\",\\n \\\"OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT\\\": f\\\"{LANGFUSE_BASE_URL}/api/public/otel\\\",\\n \\\"OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS\\\": f\\\"Authorization=Basic {langfuse_auth},x-langfuse-ingestion-version=4\\\",\\n }\\n)\\n```\\nFor more troubleshooting, see [Using Langfuse with an Existing OpenTelemetry Setup](/faq/all/existing-otel-setup#aws-bedrock-agentcore-adot).\\n## Example repository: Continuous Evaluation with AgentCore and Langfuse\\nBuilding production-grade AI agents requires more than just tracing—it demands a systematic approach to continuous improvement through experimentation, testing, and monitoring. [@aristsakpinis93](https://github.com/aristsakpinis93) has created a comprehensive [example repository](https://github.com/aristsakpinis93/agentcore-langfuse-continous-eval-loop) that demonstrates this continuous evaluation loop with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Langfuse.\\n_Continuous evaluation loop:_\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nThe repository covers three critical phases of the agent lifecycle:\\n 1. Experimentation & Hyperparameter Optimization\\n 2. QA & Testing with CI/CD\\n 3. Production Operations & Monitoring\\nPlease refer to the [README.md](https://github.com/aristsakpinis93/agentcore-langfuse-continous-eval-loop/blob/main/README.md) for more details.\\n## Resources\\n * [Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Documentation](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agents/)\\n * [Strands Agents SDK Documentation](https://strandsagents.com)\\n * [Langfuse Evaluation Documentation](/docs/evaluation/overview)\\n * [Langfuse Datasets & Experiments](/docs/evaluation/experiments/datasets)\\n * [Complete Example Repository](https://github.com/aristsakpinis93/agentcore-langfuse-continous-eval-loop)\\n* * *\\n* * *\\nLast edited 8/4/2026\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"github_issue\", \"url\": \"https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/issues/14265\", \"title\": \"[Feature Request] Instance-wide / global model cost configuration with discount factor\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Github Issue by @jordanScript created on June 15, 2026. The current state of the issue is: open\\n\\n## English 🇬🇧\\n\\n### Problem\\n\\nCurrently, model pricing in Langfuse is **project-scoped** only. Each project must individually configure custom model definitions via UI (Project Settings → Models) or API (`POST /api/public/models`). There is no way to set a global/instance-wide pricing adjustment that applies across all organizations and projects.\\n\\nIn enterprise environments with negotiated provider contracts (e.g., a global 22% discount on public model prices), this means:\\n\\n- Manually creating custom model definitions in every existing and new project\\n- Automating this via provisioning pipelines per project\\n- No single source of truth for enterprise-negotiated prices\\n- Risk of projects using public prices instead of negotiated ones\\n\\n### Proposed Solution\\n\\nAdd an **instance-wide model cost configuration** (environment variable or Instance Management API) that allows:\\n\\n1. **Global discount factor**: a single percentage (e.g., `22`) applied to all model prices across all projects in the instance.\\n \\n ```\\n LANGFUSE_MODEL_COST_GLOBAL_DISCOUNT=22\\n ```\\n\\n2. **Per-provider discount factors**: differentiated discounts by provider (e.g., Google -20%, Anthropic -25%).\\n \\n ```json\\n {\\n \\\"google\\\": 20,\\n \\\"anthropic\\\": 25,\\n \\\"openai\\\": 15\\n }\\n ```\\n\\n3. **Override at project level**: projects should still be able to set their own custom models, which would take priority over the global discount configuration.\\n\\nThis would allow enterprises like Falabella to:\\n- Configure negotiated discounts once at the instance level\\n- Have all projects automatically use corrected costs\\n- Maintain accurate cost observability without per-project configuration burden\\n\\n### Related Documentation\\n\\n- [Model Usage & Cost Tracking](https://langfuse.com/docs/model-usage-and-cost)\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n- [Custom Model Definitions](https://langfuse.com/docs/model-usage-and-cost#custom-model-definitions)\\n- [Instance Management API (EE)](https://langfuse.com/self-hosting/administration/instance-management-api)\\n\\n### Workaround\\n\\nCurrent workaround requires iterating all projects and creating custom model definitions with adjusted prices via API:\\n\\n```bash\\nPOST /api/public/models\\n{\\n \\\"modelName\\\": \\\"gemini-2.5-flash-enterprise\\\",\\n \\\"matchPattern\\\": \\\"(?i)^(gemini-2\\\\\\\\.5-flash)$\\\",\\n \\\"pricingTiers\\\": [{\\n \\\"name\\\": \\\"Standard\\\",\\n \\\"isDefault\\\": true,\\n \\\"priority\\\": 0,\\n \\\"conditions\\\": [],\\n \\\"prices\\\": { \\\"input\\\": 0.00006, \\\"output\\\": 0.00024 }\\n }]\\n}\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Español 🇪🇸\\n\\n### Problema\\n\\nActualmente, los precios de modelos en Langfuse están limitados al ámbito de **proyecto** (project-scoped). Cada proyecto debe configurar individualmente definiciones de modelos personalizadas a través de la UI (Project Settings → Models) o la API (`POST /api/public/models`). No existe una forma de establecer un ajuste de precios global/a nivel de instancia que aplique a todas las organizaciones y proyectos.\\n\\nEn entornos empresariales con contratos negociados con proveedores (ej. un descuento global del 22% sobre precios públicos), esto implica:\\n\\n- Crear manualmente definiciones de modelos personalizadas en cada proyecto existente y nuevo\\n- Automatizarlo mediante pipelines de provisioning por proyecto\\n- Ausencia de una fuente única de verdad para los precios negociados\\n- Riesgo de que proyectos usen precios públicos en lugar de los negociados\\n\\n### Solución Propuesta\\n\\nAgregar una **configuración de costos a nivel de instancia** (variable de entorno o Instance Management API) que permita:\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n1. **Factor de descuento global**: un porcentaje único (ej. `22`) aplicado a todos los precios de modelos en todos los proyectos de la instancia.\\n \\n ```\\n LANGFUSE_MODEL_COST_GLOBAL_DISCOUNT=22\\n ```\\n\\n2. **Factores de descuento por proveedor**: descuentos diferenciados por proveedor (ej. Google -20%, Anthropic -25%).\\n \\n ```json\\n {\\n \\\"google\\\": 20,\\n \\\"anthropic\\\": 25,\\n \\\"openai\\\": 15\\n }\\n ```\\n\\n3. **Sobrescritura a nivel de proyecto**: los proyectos deben poder seguir configurando sus propios modelos personalizados, los cuales tendrían prioridad sobre la configuración global.\\n\\nEsto permitiría a empresas como Falabella:\\n- Configurar descuentos negociados una sola vez a nivel de instancia\\n- Que todos los proyectos usen automáticamente costos corregidos\\n- Mantener observabilidad de costos precisa sin carga de configuración por proyecto\\n\\n### Documentación Relacionada\\n\\n- [Model Usage & Cost Tracking](https://langfuse.com/docs/model-usage-and-cost)\\n- [Custom Model Definitions](https://langfuse.com/docs/model-usage-and-cost#custom-model-definitions)\\n- [Instance Management API (EE)](https://langfuse.com/self-hosting/administration/instance-management-api)\\n\\n### Workaround actual\\n\\nEl workaround actual requiere iterar todos los proyectos y crear definiciones de modelos personalizadas con precios ajustados vía API:\\n\\n```bash\\nPOST /api/public/models\\n{\\n \\\"modelName\\\": \\\"gemini-2.5-flash-enterprise\\\",\\n \\\"matchPattern\\\": \\\"(?i)^(gemini-2\\\\\\\\.5-flash)$\\\",\\n \\\"pricingTiers\\\": [{\\n \\\"name\\\": \\\"Standard\\\",\\n \\\"isDefault\\\": true,\\n \\\"priority\\\": 0,\\n \\\"conditions\\\": [],\\n \\\"prices\\\": { \\\"input\\\": 0.00006, \\\"output\\\": 0.00024 }\\n }]\\n}\\n```\\n---\\nComment #1 by @Babar-maker76:\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nThe discount/markup configuration request points at a broader gap: teams need per-model cost visibility at the execution level, not just aggregate billing. Instance-wide pricing config is the right foundation, but the most actionable layer is per-run cost attribution so you can see exactly which agent run, which model call, and which workflow step drove a cost spike.\\n\\nFor teams running multiple models (e.g. GPT-4o for orchestration, GPT-4o-mini for subagents), the billing surprise usually comes from a token anomaly on a specific model that was supposed to use the cheaper option. Without per-execution cost logging, you see the bill but not the cause.\\n\\nWe built per-execution cost tracking into AI Agents Control Tower (agents.opsveritas.com) with support for 60+ model pricing tables and alerts at 3x baseline cost per run. Happy to compare notes on the pricing config approach if useful.\\n\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"github_discussion\", \"url\": \"https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/11610\", \"title\": \"How can I use LangFuse to visualize and analyze the trace data like PowerBI (stack bar charts, slicers, etc)\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Title: How can I use LangFuse to visualize and analyze the trace data like PowerBI (stack bar charts, slicers, etc)\\nCategory: Support\\nAuthor: @Sourav-xd\\nTimestamp: January 19, 2026\\nBody:\\n### Describe your question\\n\\nHow can Langfuse be used to visualize and analyze trace data in a BI-like way, similar to Power BI? Is it possible to create advanced visualizations such as stacked or grouped bar charts using two dimensions (e.g. model × environment, status × time) within a single vertical bar chart? Additionally, are there plans or best practices for applying interactive slicers or global filters (model, environment, metadata, time range, etc.) to dynamically explore trace data across all dashboard visualizations?\\n\\n### Langfuse Cloud or Self-Hosted?\\n\\nSelf-Hosted\\n\\n### If Self-Hosted\\n\\nNew minor version: v3.147.0\\n\\n### If Langfuse Cloud\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### SDK and integration versions\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### Pre-Submission Checklist\\n\\n- [X] I have checked for existing issues/discussions and consulted Langfuse AI.\\nComments:\\n\\n Comment #1 from @inkeep-ai-assistant on January 19, 2026:\\n\\n \\n\\n Langfuse provides customizable dashboards for visualizing and analyzing trace data directly within the UI[(1)](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards). You can create personalized views to track metrics like latency, cost, quality monitoring, and user behavior[(1)](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards).\\n\\n## Current Visualization Capabilities\\n\\nLangfuse custom dashboards support multiple chart types including line charts, bar charts, time series, and pie charts[(1)](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards). You can create widgets that:\\n\\n- Choose from traces, observations, or evaluation scores as data sources[(1)](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards)\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n- Select metrics to measure (count, latency, cost, scores, etc.)[(1)](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards)\\n- Group by dimensions like user, model, time, trace name[(1)](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards)\\n- Apply filters to narrow down specific data subsets[(1)](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards)\\n\\nThe dashboards support advanced filtering including metadata filters, time-based filters, user properties, model parameters, tags and labels, and score thresholds[(1)](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards).\\n\\n## Current Limitations for BI-Like Features\\n\\nBased on the available sources, there are some limitations compared to full BI tools:\\n\\n**Stacked/Grouped Bar Charts**: The documentation mentions bar charts as an available chart type for comparing values across categories[(1)](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards), but does not explicitly describe stacked or grouped bar charts with multiple dimensions within a single visualization.\\n\\n**Metadata as Dimensions**: Currently, custom metadata fields cannot be directly selected as dimensions in dashboard widgets[(2)](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/7577). This is a known limitation - the feature was initially planned but cut due to complexity in using metadata at scale in dashboards[(2)](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/7577).\\n\\n**Interactive Slicers**: The documentation does not describe global filters or interactive slicers that apply across all dashboard visualizations simultaneously.\\n\\n## Alternative Approaches\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/docs/evaluation/core-concepts\", \"title\": \"Core Concepts\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Concepts - Langfuse\\n[Docs](/docs)\\n[Evaluation](/docs/evaluation/overview)\\n[Concepts](/docs/evaluation/core-concepts)\\n# Core Concepts\\nThis page digs into the different concepts of evaluations, and what's available in Langfuse.\\nIf you are still deciding _what_ to measure, [Choosing what to evaluate in the Langfuse Academy](/academy/evaluate/choosing-what-to-evaluate) works through how to turn observed failures into a small set of metrics, and [Writing good evaluators](/academy/evaluate/writing-evaluators) covers how to make those checks trustworthy.\\nReady to start?\\n * [Create a dataset](/docs/evaluation/experiments/datasets) to measure your LLM application's performance consistently\\n * [Run an experiment](/docs/evaluation/core-concepts#experiments) to get an overview of how your application is doing\\n * [Set up LLM-as-a-Judge](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/llm-as-a-judge) to evaluate your live traces\\n * [Create a code evaluator](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/code-evaluators) for deterministic checks\\n## The Evaluation Loop\\nLLM applications often have a constant [loop of testing and monitoring](/academy/ai-engineering-loop).\\n**[Offline evaluation](/academy/evaluate)** lets you test your application against a fixed dataset before you deploy. You run your new prompt or model against test cases, review the scores, iterate until the results look good, then deploy your changes. In Langfuse, you can do that by running [Experiments](/docs/evaluation/core-concepts#experiments).\\n**[Online evaluation](/academy/monitoring)** scores live traces to catch issues in real traffic. When you find edge cases your dataset didn't cover, you add them back to your dataset so future experiments will catch them.\\nDeploy\\n[OnlineTracetraces · sessions · agents · prompts](/academy/tracing)\\n[OnlineMonitordashboards · LLM-as-judge · feedback](/academy/monitoring)\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n[OfflineBuild datasetsdatasets · features-as-tests](/academy/datasets)\\n[OfflineExperimentprompts · models · code variants](/academy/experiments)\\n[OfflineEvaluatejudges · custom evals · annotation](/academy/evaluate)\\n> **Here's an example workflow** for building a customer support chatbot\\n> \\n> 1. You update your prompt to make responses less formal.\\n> 2. Before deploying, you run an **experiment** : test the new prompt against your dataset of customer questions **(offline evaluation)**.\\n> 3. You review the scores and outputs. The tone improved, but responses are longer and some miss important links.\\n> 4. You refine the prompt and run the experiment again.\\n> 5. The results look good now. You deploy the new prompt to production.\\n> 6. You monitor with **online evaluation** to catch any new edge cases.\\n> 7. You notice that a customer asked a question in French, but the bot responded in English.\\n> 8. You add this French query to your dataset so future experiments will catch this issue.\\n> 9. You update your prompt to support French responses and run another experiment.\\n> \\n> \\n> Over time, your dataset grows from a couple of examples to a diverse, representative set of real-world test cases.\\n## Scores\\n[Scores](/docs/evaluation/scores/overview) are Langfuse's universal data object for storing evaluation results. Any time you want to assign a quality judgment to an LLM output, whether by a human annotation, an LLM judge, a programmatic check, or end-user feedback, the result is stored as a score.\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nTo use an LLM-as-a-Judge evaluator for batch evaluation, enable the [Langfuse v4 preview](/docs/v4) toggle for the evaluator. To use the same evaluator on newly ingested data in real time, upgrade to Python SDK ≥ 4.7.0 or JS/TS SDK ≥ 5.4.0. If you ingest directly via OTEL, [set `x-langfuse-ingestion-version: 4` on your OTEL span exporter](/integrations/native/opentelemetry#real-time-ingestion).\\n 1. Open the Traces table.\\n 2. Filter to the timeframe and trace criteria you want to evaluate.\\n 3. Select the matching rows.\\n 4. Click Actions → Evaluate.\\n 5. Choose an evaluator and run it on the selected traces.\\nThe resulting scores are attached to the matching observations in each selected trace.\\n## Experiments\\nAn experiment runs your application against a dataset and evaluates the outputs. This is how you test changes before deploying to production.\\n### Definitions\\nBefore diving into experiments, it's helpful to understand the building blocks in Langfuse: datasets, dataset items, tasks, scores, and experiments.\\nObject| Definition \\n---|--- \\n **Dataset**| A collection of test cases (dataset items). You can run experiments on a dataset. \\n **Dataset item**| One item in a dataset. Each dataset item contains an input (the scenario to test) and optionally an expected output. \\n **Task**| The application code that you want to test in an experiment. This will be performed on each dataset item, and you will score the output. \"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"**Evaluation Method**| A function that scores experiment results. In the context of a Langfuse experiment, this can be a [code evaluator](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/code-evaluators), a score ingested from your own code via [API/SDK](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/scores-via-sdk), or [LLM-as-a-Judge](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/llm-as-a-judge). \\n **Score**| The output of an evaluation. See Scores for the available data types and details. \\n **Experiment Run**| A single execution of your task against all items in a dataset, producing outputs (and scores). \\n \\nYou can find the data model for these objects [here](/docs/evaluation/experiments/data-model).\\n### How these work together\\nThis is what happens conceptually:\\nWhen you run an experiment on a given **dataset** , each of the **dataset items** will be passed to the **task function** you defined. The task function is generally an LLM call that happens in your application, that you want to test. The task function produces an output for each dataset item. This process is called an **experiment run**. The resulting collection of outputs linked to the dataset items are the **experiment results**.\\nOften, you want to score these experiment results. You can use various evaluation methods that take in the dataset item and the output produced by the task function, and produce a score based on criteria you define. Based on these scores, you can then get a complete picture of how your application performs across all test cases.\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nYou can compare experiment runs to see if a new prompt version improves scores, or identify specific inputs where your application struggles. Based on these experiment results, you can decide whether the change is ready to be deployed to production.\\nYou can find more details on how these objects link together under the hood on the [data model page](/docs/evaluation/experiments/data-model).\\n### Two ways to run experiments\\nYou can **run experiments programmatically using the Langfuse SDK**. This gives you full control over the task, evaluation logic, and more. [Learn more about running experiments via SDK](/docs/evaluation/experiments/experiments-via-sdk).\\nAnother way is to **run experiments directly from the Langfuse interface** by selecting a dataset and prompt version. This is useful for quick iterations on prompts without writing code. [Learn more about running experiments via UI](/docs/evaluation/experiments/experiments-via-ui).\\n**Langfuse Execution**\\n **Local/CI Execution**\\n **Langfuse Dataset**\\n[Experiments via UI](/docs/evaluation/experiments/experiments-via-ui)\\n[Experiments via SDK](/docs/evaluation/experiments/experiments-via-sdk)\\n **Local Dataset**\\nNot supported\\n[Experiments via SDK](/docs/evaluation/experiments/experiments-via-sdk)\\n_While it's optional, we recommend managing the underlying[Datasets](/docs/evaluation/experiments/datasets) in Langfuse as it allows for [1] In-UI comparison tables of different experiments on the same data and [2] Iteratively improve dataset based on production/staging traces._\\n* * *\\n* * *\\nLast edited 8/31/2026\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}]}"}
